2.w: “Without a doubt you are the people, and wisdom will die with you.

3.w: I also have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?

4.w: I am a laughingstock to my friends, I, who called on God and whom he answered — a righteous and blameless man is a laughingstock!

5.w: For calamity, there is derision (according to the ideas of the fortunate)— a fate for those whose feet slip.

6.w: But the tents of robbers are peaceful, and those who provoke God are confident — who carry their god in their hands.

7.w: “But now, ask the animals and they will teach you, or the birds of the sky and they will tell you.

8.w: Or speak to the earth and it will teach you, or let the fish of the sea declare to you.

9.w: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the Lord has done this?

10.w: In his hand is the life of every creature and the breath of all the human race.

11.w: Does not the ear test words, as the tongue tastes food?

12.w: Is not wisdom found among the aged? Does not long life bring understanding?

13.w: With God are wisdom and power; counsel and understanding are his.

14.w: If he tears down, it cannot be rebuilt; if he imprisons a person, there is no escape.

15.w: If he holds back the waters, then they dry up; if he releases them, they destroy the land.

16.w: With him are strength and prudence; both the one who goes astray and the one who misleads are his.

17.w: He leads counselors away stripped and makes judges into fools.

18.w: He loosens the bonds of kings and binds a loincloth around their waist.

19.w: He leads priests away stripped and overthrows the potentates.

20.w: He deprives the trusted advisers of speech and takes away the discernment of elders.

21.w: He pours contempt on noblemen and disarms the powerful.

22.w: He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadows into the light.

23.w: He makes nations great and destroys them; he extends the boundaries of nations and disperses them.

24.w: He deprives the leaders of the earth of their understanding; he makes them wander in a trackless desert waste.

25.w: They grope about in darkness without light; he makes them stagger like drunkards.
